rows.name: Hydro One Networks Inc.
rows.publisher: Hydro One Networks Inc.; Ontario Energy Board filing EB-2021-0110
rows.method: Unplanned transmission interruptions, normalized by the annual system peak.
rows.scope: Transmission; unplanned interruptions at all delivery points; annual energy not supplied normalized against system peak. This is not MWh.
rows.evidence: Published December 30, 2025. PDF page 16, transmitter scorecard MD&A page 4 of 10, reports actual 8.2 system minutes for 2024 versus target 8.8. The corresponding annual system peak denominator is not supplied in this scorecard; no raw ENS conversion is justified.
rows.definition: ENS-N is energy not supplied expressed as equivalent minutes at system peak. It is not MWh, and it cannot be divided by distribution customer accounts to obtain AENS.

rows.name: Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro
rows.publisher: Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro; filing to the Board of Commissioners of Public Utilities
rows.method: Published interrupted energy in MW-min. Divide by 60 for MWh; no annual customer-normalized estimate is inferred.
rows.scope: Historical annual subset: undersupplied energy from under-frequency load-shedding events only. Not total annual utility ENS; do not map to Newfoundland Power as its own network performance.
rows.evidence: PDF page 106 (printed KPI page 26), Table 15: UFLS Undersupplied Energy, total events, 12 Months-to-Date 2019 = 191 MW-min. The 2018 full-year comparator is 6464 MW-min. Unit-only conversion of 191/60 gives 3.183333333 MWh. No matched denominator for utility-wide AENS.
rows.definition: This is a historical record from Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro, a different utility from Newfoundland Power. Its scope is limited to the identified events.

rows.name: Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro
rows.publisher: Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro; filing to the Board of Commissioners of Public Utilities
rows.method: Published interrupted energy in MW-min. Divide by 60 for MWh; no annual customer-normalized estimate is inferred.
rows.scope: Historical single transmission event at Doyles Terminal Station, affecting 5292 downstream Newfoundland Power customers. Not annual ENS.
rows.evidence: PDF page 124 (Appendix C page C-4), Event 10: 1607 MW-min energy unsupplied from a transformer T1 protection issue, outage duration 5 hours 47 minutes. Conversion 1607/60 = 26.783333333 MWh. Affected customers are not a valid denominator for annual utility-wide AENS.
rows.definition: This is a historical record from Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro, a different utility from Newfoundland Power. Its scope is limited to the identified events.

coverage.name: Ontario Energy Board
coverage.note: OEB annual scorecards and customer-account releases update automatically. Regulatory filings add measures such as momentary interruptions.

coverage.name: Régie de l’énergie
coverage.note: Régie filings include Hydro-Québec continuity and restoration measures. Voltage levels and event exclusions differ between indices.

coverage.name: New Brunswick Energy and Utilities Board
coverage.note: Board proceedings and NB Power reports provide complementary evidence. Corporate rolling-average KPIs are kept separate from single-year outage measures.

coverage.name: British Columbia Utilities Commission
coverage.note: BC Hydro publishes all-event and normalized indices. Transmission delivery-point measures are shown separately.

coverage.name: Alberta Utilities Commission
coverage.note: AUC service-quality reports and Rule 002 are the provincial reporting route. Distribution companies and electricity retailers have different customer populations.

coverage.name: Saskatchewan Rate Review Panel
coverage.note: The Rate Review Panel advises government on rates. SaskPower’s annual report supplies separately labelled utility reliability measures.

coverage.name: Manitoba Public Utilities Board
coverage.note: The Public Utilities Board hosts rate proceedings. Manitoba Hydro’s annual measures retain their reported period and method.

coverage.name: Nova Scotia Energy Board
coverage.note: The Nova Scotia Energy Board oversees utility reporting. NSP publishes repeated-interruption and long-duration customer measures; municipal utilities remain separate.

coverage.name: Newfoundland and Labrador Board of Commissioners of Public Utilities
coverage.note: The PUB publishes utility filings. Newfoundland Power and Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro are different systems and their results are not combined.

coverage.name: Island Regulatory and Appeals Commission
coverage.note: IRAC regulates Maritime Electric. Summerside Electric generally has separate arrangements, so Maritime Electric figures do not represent the whole province.

coverage.name: Yukon Utilities Board
coverage.note: Yukon Energy and ATCO Electric Yukon are separate utilities. The reviewed Yukon Energy index treats ATCO and its downstream customers as one wholesale customer.

coverage.name: Northwest Territories Public Utilities Board
coverage.note: The territorial PUB oversees utility proceedings. NTPC’s outage measures are not applied to other Northwest Territories distributors.

coverage.name: Nunavut Utility Rates Review Council
coverage.note: The Utility Rates Review Council advises government. Qulliq operates community systems; published community context remains separate from outage indices.

CAIFI.summary: No customer-affected CAIFI observation or matched distinct-customer denominator was verified in the reviewed Canadian sources. Circuit-average frequency and CAIDI are different indices.

sources.title: NB Power: published KPI definitions and limitations

AENS.summary: The reviewed ENS records do not include a matching annual customer denominator. Transmission delivery points and downstream household accounts are different populations. Dividing these values would create an unsupported annual AENS estimate.
